Economies of scale of biogas production using food waste. 2.2.3 Woody and Select MSW Biomass HC Production Estimates Woody type of biomass (woody biomass and select MSW) is dried to a moisture content of 10 wt % and fed to an indirect gasifier, where biomass deconstructs to tars, chars, and raw syngas (CO , CO, and H ). Char is combusted to provide heat for the gasifier. The clean syngas stream 2 2 is then converted to fuels via FT synthesis and separated into gasoline-, jet-, and diesel-range products via distillation. Light end products from FT synthesis are recycled, and either combusted for process fuel or converted back to syngas in the tar reformer. A more detailed description of the process design is provided elsewhere (Dutta and Phillips 2009; Swanson et al. 2010; Dutta et al. 2012, 2014; Tan et al. 2015), and products are often called FT-SPK. In the FT-SPK pathway (ASTM D7566 Annex A1), woody biomass is converted to syngas (from biologic or petrochemical sources) using gasification, then to jet fuel components using the FT synthesis reaction. Feedstocks for this pathway are from various sources of renewable biomass, with a focus mainly on woody biomass such as MSW, agricultural and forest wastes, wood, and energy crops. This pathway was approved by ASTM in June 2009 with a 50% blend limit. Figure 18 illustrates this process concept. The overall yield of the process is 71 gge/dry ton from woody biomass feedstock to hydrocarbon fuels.
